cases.sentence: Напротив, никогда, в самых лучших ___, войско не представляло более веселого, оживленного зрелища.
cases.explain: «материальных условиях» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: On the contrary, the army had never under the best material conditions presented a more cheerful and animated aspect. This was because all who began to grow depressed or who lost strength were sifted out of the army day by day. All the physically or morally weak had long since been left behind and only the flower of the army—physically and mentally—remained.

cases.sentence: В ___, пригородившей плетень, собралось больше всего народа.
cases.explain: «осьмой роте» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: More men collected behind the wattle fence of the Eighth Company than anywhere else. Two sergeants major were sitting with them and their campfire blazed brighter than others. For leave to sit by their wattle they demanded contributions of fuel.

cases.sentence: Неси дров-то, — кричал один краснорожий, ___, щурившийся и мигавший от дыма, но не отодвигавшийся от огня.
cases.explain: «рыжий солдат» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Eh, Makéev! What has become of you, you son of a bitch? Are you lost or have the wolves eaten you? Fetch some more wood!” shouted a red-haired and red-faced man, screwing up his eyes and blinking because of the smoke but not moving back from the fire. “And you, Jackdaw, go and fetch some wood!” said he to another soldier. This red-haired man was neither a sergeant nor a corporal, but being robust he ordered about those weaker than himself. The soldier they called “Jackdaw,” a thin little fellow with a sharp nose, rose obediently and was about to go but at that instant there came into the light of the fire the slender, handsome figure of a young soldier carrying a load of wood.

cases.sentence: Рыжий был не унтер-офицер и не ефрейтор, но был ___, и потому повелевал теми, которые были слабее его.
cases.explain: «здоровый солдат» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Eh, Makéev! What has become of you, you son of a bitch? Are you lost or have the wolves eaten you? Fetch some more wood!” shouted a red-haired and red-faced man, screwing up his eyes and blinking because of the smoke but not moving back from the fire. “And you, Jackdaw, go and fetch some wood!” said he to another soldier. This red-haired man was neither a sergeant nor a corporal, but being robust he ordered about those weaker than himself. The soldier they called “Jackdaw,” a thin little fellow with a sharp nose, rose obediently and was about to go but at that instant there came into the light of the fire the slender, handsome figure of a young soldier carrying a load of wood.

cases.sentence: — Ах, маменька, ___, да хороша, да в мушкатера...
cases.explain: «холодная роса» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Mother! The dew is cold but clear. … It’s well that I’m a musketeer …” he sang, pretending to hiccup after each syllable.

cases.sentence: — И то, брат, — сказал он; и сев, достал из ранца обрывок французского ___ и стал обвертывать им ногу.
cases.explain: «синего сукна» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Right enough, friend,” said he, and, having sat down, took out of his knapsack a scrap of blue French cloth, and wrapped it round his foot. “It’s the steam that spoils them,” he added, stretching out his feet toward the fire.

cases.sentence: Говорят, перебьем до конца, тогда всем по ___.
cases.explain: «двойному товару» — after the preposition «по», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “They’ll soon be issuing us new ones. They say that when we’ve finished hammering them, we’re to receive double kits!”

cases.sentence: — А вишь, ___ Петров, отстал-таки, — сказал фельдфебель.
cases.explain: «сукин сын» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “And that son of a bitch Petróv has lagged behind after all, it seems,” said one sergeant major.

cases.sentence: — А в ___, сказывали, за вчерашний день девять человек не досчитали.
cases.explain: «третьей роте» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “But in the Third Company they say nine men were missing yesterday.”

cases.sentence: — А в третьей роте, сказывали, за ___ девять человек не досчитали.
cases.explain: «вчерашний день» — after the preposition «за», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “But in the Third Company they say nine men were missing yesterday.”

cases.sentence: — сказал ___, с упреком обращаясь к тому, который сказал, что ноги зазнобил.
cases.explain: «старый солдат» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Do you want to be doing the same?” said an old soldier, turning reproachfully to the man who had spoken of frozen feet.

cases.explain: «чистый народ» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “But they’re a clean folk, lads,” the first man went on; “he was white—as white as birchbark—and some of them are such fine fellows, you might think they were nobles.”

cases.explain: «старый солдат» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “That was a real battle,” said an old soldier. “It’s the only one worth remembering; but since that … it’s only been tormenting folk.”

cases.sentence: — Все одно конец сделаем, не будет ходить, — зевая сказал ___.
cases.explain: «старый солдат» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Well, anyhow we’re going to end it. He won’t come here again,” remarked the old soldier, yawning.

cases.sentence: Скажи, бабы холсты разложили, — сказал солдат, любуясь на ___.
cases.explain: «млечный путь» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Look at the stars. It’s wonderful how they shine! You would think the women had spread out their linen,” said one of the men, gazing with admiration at the Milky Way.

cases.explain: «урожайному году» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “That’s a sign of a good harvest next year.”

cases.sentence: — Вишь грохочут в ___, — сказал один солдат.
cases.explain: «пятой роте» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Hark at them roaring there in the Fifth Company!” said one of the soldiers, “and what a lot of them there are!”

cases.sentence: Один солдат поднялся и пошел к ___.
cases.explain: «пятой роте» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: One of the men got up and went over to the Fifth Company.

cases.explain: «пятой роте» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “Oh, I’ll go across and have a look. …” And several of the men went over to the Fifth Company.
